System power (usually shows the shutdown dialog)
Momentary layer: active while held. LT (tap a key, hold a layer) is not a separate Oryx code: it is tap = key + hold = MO(n), written LT(n, KC_x) in keyloom
Toggle layer: tap to turn on, tap again to turn off. Put a TG to the same layer on the layer itself so the user can leave
Switch to layer: turns that layer on and every other layer (except the default) off. TO(0) is the universal way home
Tap-toggle: hold for momentary, tap (QMK default: 5 taps, Oryx may differ) to toggle on. Uses tap-hold timing
One-shot layer: the next key press comes from that layer, then it turns off
Set default (base) layer until power-off. Not yet seen in a real Oryx layout: check Oryx offers it before relying on it
Layer-tap, written LT(layer, KC_x): tap sends the key, hold switches to the layer. Not an Oryx code: stored as tap = key + hold = MO(layer). (The '<' key is KC_LT.)
Mod-tap, written MT(LCTL, KC_x) or LCTL_T(KC_x): tap sends the key, hold is the modifier. Not an Oryx code: stored as tap = key + hold = modifier. Oryx mod-taps take one modifier
Tap one key, hold another, written TAP_HOLD(KC_x, KC_y); `_` leaves a side empty. Oryx compiles it to a custom dual-function key
Meh (Ctrl+Alt+Shift) as a hold action: tap = key, hold = Meh. Oryx compiles it to MEH_T(KC_x)
Hyper (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+GUI) as a hold action: tap = key, hold = Hyper. Assumed to mirror MEH_T; not yet seen in a real Oryx layout

One-shot modifier family: the modifier applies to the next key only. Not supported by keyloom yet (OSM(...) is rejected): Oryx offers one-shot modifiers but how it stores them isn't confirmed, so they are set by hand in Oryx
Turn the RGB lighting on or off
Static (solid) lighting mode; ZSA's code for 'show the layer colors' set in Oryx
ZSA: set all LEDs to one color; the color is the action's `color` field (e.g. #ffab00)
ZSA: turn the per-layer colors from Oryx on or off
ZSA: cycle the brightness of the status LEDs. Not yet seen in a real layout
ZSA Navigator: hold for fast pointer movement. Not yet seen in a real layout
ZSA Navigator: hold for slow, precise pointer movement. Not yet seen in a real layout
ZSA Navigator: while held, the trackball scrolls instead of moving the pointer
ZSA Navigator: toggle scroll mode for the trackball
ZSA macOS key: Launchpad. Not yet seen in a real layout
ZSA macOS key: Spotlight search. Not yet seen in a real layout
ZSA macOS key: toggle Do Not Disturb / Focus. Not yet seen in a real layout
ZSA macOS key: lock the screen. Not yet seen in a real layout
ZSA macOS key: start dictation. Not yet seen in a real layout
Reboot into the bootloader for flashing. Keep it on a hard-to-hit spot of a rarely used layer
Layer lock: keep the current layer on after releasing its MO/LT key; press again (or TO) to unlock. Useful on mouse and nav layers
Caps Word: capitalise until a non-word key (space, punctuation). Not yet seen in a real layout
Repeat the last key. Not yet seen in a real layout
Alternate repeat (the 'opposite' of the last key). Not yet seen in a real layout
Type out the current tapping term in ms. Not yet seen in a real layout
Raise the tapping term by 5 ms. Not yet seen in a real layout
Lower the tapping term by 5 ms. Not yet seen in a real layout
Transparent: falls through to the next active lower layer. A blank key in Oryx compiles to this too
No action: the key does nothing and blocks fall-through. Use it on gaming layers instead of transparent where the base has tap-hold keys
